title: The Standing Register — which institutions are officially permitted to enrol international students, every dated edition kept
description:
The worldwide record of which institutions are officially permitted to enrol international students: what the official registers say, what they used to say, and what changed. Every edition of each source register is fetched on a schedule, hashed, and kept after the authority deletes or overwrites it. Registers held: Australia (CRICOS, Department of Education), Canada (designated learning institutions, IRCC — change record only, Crown copyright), Japan (MEXT accredited institutions), United Kingdom (register of licensed student sponsors, Home Office).

Each release packages the published layer per register: the current register, the dated change record, the archive index with every edition's SHA-256 digests, and — where the witness layer has run — OpenTimestamps proofs anchoring those digests in the Bitcoin block chain and Internet Archive captures of each edition at its immutable commit URL.

A row leaving a register is not evidence of wrongdoing. Registers publish a status, not a cause. An entry can leave through withdrawal, merger, rename, voluntary surrender, corporate restructure, lapse at renewal, or a correction by the publisher; the source does not say which, and neither does this record.

Our own outputs are CC BY 4.0. Each source register's own licence and attribution travel inside its files, and are reproduced in every archive.
